source: docs/slice-vs-stock-2026-10-23.md (§6-§8, pre-registered). svs_report.py evaluates this file; run_ab.py reads the arm structure and the step-cap mode from it; prepare reads the declared dump rows. The doc is the normative text.

structure._note: Manipulation checks per cell (run_ab.py validity) and per template home (prepare). stock is the host's own headless composition plus the neutral overlay; slice adds the plugin's one row (dsh plugin add); stock-compact is stock with compaction-basic's trigger and retained tail moved (profile/stock-compact.patch.yml). Every arm keeps compaction, the pruner and spill at its composition's settings, so compaction events are allowed and recorded, not a validity failure. "fold": false in every arm (pre-freeze fix, 2026-10-23): r3's fold of its turn-1 read is a reported manipulation check (metrics in_turn fold_of_read), not a validity condition; r3's validity is its T1 delivery, the same in every arm.

unit.pairing: same task and rep index; the cells of a (task, rep) group ran back to back, one cell at a time, the first arm rotating with (rep - 1 + seed); the content of a seeded task (f1) is identical across the arms of a group

min_pairs._note: Of 23 planned (task, rep) pairs and 23 planned memory items (f1: 4 items x 2 pairs; r1-r5: 1 item x 3 pairs). Below a minimum the dependent quantity is 'insufficient'.

cell_counts_only_if: every turn exited 0 or ended with a model-attributable turn_end (the harness step cap 'blocked', 'max-tokens', or 'error' with a code outside the infra list, CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED included); never an infra error, a missing turn_end, a harness timeout or a budget kill

system prompt and slice tool fingerprints equal the arm's entry in fingerprints.json; the arm's tool count (stock and stock-compact 12, slice 16); slice's tools are stock's plus the four recall tools; one tool list and one system prompt for the whole session
one turn per prompt: user prompts = turn ends = prompts, no goal-round messages
the system prompt contains no /private or /Users
slice: tape header short (76 or 78 chars) and tool lines long, as main ships; stock arms: no slice tape entry
isolation: no blocked path changed mode, inode or ctime while a turn ran; no worktree change during the cell

delivery, the same in every arm: r1, r2, r3, r4 (meta; r3: its T1 read carries the exam's fact, whether or not a fold condenses it later) and f1 (truth sidecar: T3 build id, T5 lint message) show the fact in a non-recall tool result of the delivery turn
reported, not a validity condition: r3's fold of its turn-1 read in slice (a manipulation check; before 2026-10-23 it was required in slice only, which made the validity rule asymmetric)
paid runs: every sibling entry of the A/B root's parent directory (the session scratchpad) except symlinks is blocked while a turn runs (run_ab.py enforces it; the list is in the manifest)
validity.pair_rule: a (task, rep) pair counts for a comparison only when both of its cells are valid; dropped pairs are listed
validity.memory_exclusion: a pair drops from the memory comparison when, in either cell, a tool call up to the last exam turn was flagged (outside the workdir, session log, truth sidecar, harness, vault, key location, disk search), or an answer-sufficient token leaked before the exam turn into assistant text or a file-writing tool input, or an exam answer arrived through a non-recall tool result before the model wrote it (oracle via the file system). It still counts for success and cost.

P1_cost.metric: cost (off-peak sheet; peak is exactly 2x every field, so ratios do not depend on the sheet), billed tokens of every loop request, failed attempt and compaction summarizer call
P1_cost.R_t: per task: sum of slice cost / sum of stock cost over the task's valid pairs
P1_cost.N: geometric mean of R_t over the seven short sessions: five short recall sessions r1-r5 and two coding sessions c1, c2 (each task weighs the same)
P1_cost.N_recall_N_coding: secondary, never decisive: the geometric mean over r1-r5 and over c1, c2 alone
P1_cost.G: geometric mean of R_t over all eight tasks (reported)
also_reported: sum ratio over all valid pairs (dollar-weighted)
per task: median paired ratio, min and max

P2_success.dS: sum of pass(slice) - sum of pass(stock) over all valid pairs

P3_memory.items: f1: build_id, lint_error, deploy, trap (verify info memory_items); r1-r5: the exam (verify pass)
P3_memory.dM: correct items(slice) - correct items(stock) over memory-eligible pairs
P3_memory.dB: bad items(slice) - bad items(stock): wrong, decoy, stale, hedged, confabulated (CANNOT-RECOVER and missing are honest misses, not bad)

quality_floor._note: Q holds iff dS >= -1, no task with dS_t <= -2, dM >= -1 and dB <= +1.

quality_better._note: slice better: dS >= +2 or dM >= +2 (with Q holding).

rules.if: any minimum not met (or L or N not computable)
Q holds and L <= 0.80 and N <= 1.10
Q holds and slice better and L <= 1.00 and N <= 1.10
otherwise (including L <= 0.80 with N > 1.10: a long-session saving bought with short-session overhead)

decision.order: rules are applied top to bottom; the first that matches decides (the same order as the record's §7 and svs_report.verdict)

arbitration.trigger: before pooling, if any minimum is not met, or the verdict would change when L or N moved by 0.05 in either direction, or Q is decided at its margin (dS = -1 or -2, some dS_t = -1 or -2, dM = -1 or -2, dB = +1 or +2), or 'slice better' is at its margin where it matters: Q holds, rule 3 does not decide, L <= 1.00 and N <= 1.10 (rule 4's cost conditions, which the L/N band test covers), and max(dS, dM) is +1 or +2
arbitration.decide_on: the pooled batches, the same rules and thresholds, minimums unchanged; no band test and no second arbitration
arbitration.budget_condition: only if ledger spend + the arbitration estimate stays below the cap minus the reserve; otherwise the batch verdict stands, marked unarbitrated

secondary._note: Reported, never decisive: stock-compact against stock and against slice with the same P1-P3 quantities; compaction summaries, failures and prunes per cell with their turns; post-compaction memory failures (exam items failed in cells whose history was compacted or pruned before the exam turn); context-limit errors; peak and mean request size; cache hit rate; requests and steps per turn; wall time; same-turn re-reads (success-only mutations); native spills; slice folds.
